rules.rule: General-service incandescent and halogen incandescent bulbs below the 45 lumens-per-watt efficiency standard may no longer be manufactured or sold; general-service LED/CFL bulbs required instead. Appliance lamps, 3-way bulbs, plant lights, and other specialty/exempt categories (e.g., refrigerator, black-light, bug, colored, traffic-signal lamps) are excluded.
Import and sale of inefficient 75W and 100W incandescent general-service bulbs banned.
Manufacture/import of inefficient 40W and 60W incandescent general-service bulbs banned (existing retail inventory could still be sold through).
Progressive EU-wide phase-out of general-purpose (non-directional) incandescent bulbs; did not initially cover reflector/spotlight or halogen bulbs.
Non-directional halogen bulbs (candle, GLS, globe, golf ball) phased out under EU Ecodesign Directive EC 244/2009 (delayed from 2016).
Low-voltage (G4, GY6.35) and high-voltage (G9) halogen lamps phased out under the EU Ecodesign Regulation; special-purpose halogen capsules, R7s linear lamps, fridge/oven lamps exempted.
UK continued the EU-derived halogen/incandescent phase-out schedule after leaving the EU, applying the same 2018 and 2023 non-directional and directional halogen cut-off dates domestically.

NOM-028-ENER-2010 phased out general-use incandescent lamps in three stages: 100W+ from 31 Dec 2011, 75W+ from 31 Dec 2012, and 60W/40W (all remaining wattages) could no longer be sold from 1 Jan 2015.
